key_insight: OMatG-FC generates inorganic crystals by learning atomic species and cell volume on fixed structural frameworks, achieving a reported state-of-the-art stable, unique, and novel (S.U.N.) rate below the convex hull.
engineering_relevance: Fixing atomic packing reduces the generation problem’s dimensionality while retaining flexibility to discover unseen stable prototypes from known frameworks.
method: Condition generation on fixed fractional coordinates and unit-volume lattice vectors.
Use discrete flow matching for atomic species and stochastic interpolants for cell-volume scaling.
Identify duplicate frameworks in MP-20 and provide a framework-split dataset.
evidence_signal: Evaluation uses LeMat-GenBench with three ML interatomic potentials; the abstract reports state-of-the-art S.U.N. performance but gives no numerical rates.
watch_item: Fixed-framework conditioning limits exploration of new atomic packings, and predicted stability still requires validation beyond ML interatomic potentials.
